feedback.problem: Find the volume of the solid region enclosed by the $xz$-plane and the surface $y=z{e}^{x},$ and the planes $x=-1,$ $x=0,$ $z=0,$ $z=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that our solid can be written as a type III region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le z{e}^{x}}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z{e}^{x}}dy\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}[y]_{y=0}^{y=z{e}^{x}}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}z{e}^{x}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{e}^{x}{[\frac{1}{2}{z}^{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}\frac{1}{2}{e}^{x}\,dx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[{e}^{x}]_{x=-1}^{x=0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{0}-{e}^{-1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1-\frac{1}{e}) \\  & =\frac{e-1}{2e}\end{aligned}
$$
